data.situation:
On the way out, Maya stopped at the evacuation plan on the corridor wall. The centre was preparing a supervised drill, and the organiser pointed to the designated route on the building's own plan. Participants would practise leaving together when asked to evacuate; the exercise was not an emergency. A visitor who had missed the explanation became angry about the temporary interruption. Noor tried to pacify him by listening to his concern and explaining when the room would reopen. She did not promise that his complaint would change the drill. On the reception desk lay an archive report about an outbreak of violence at an old public meeting. Maya asked why that report had been left beside the drill register. Noor moved it back into the exhibition folder. The report concerned a historical incident; it did not describe a present danger or the reason for today's drill. Scheduled drill
The organiser will explain the exercise and the designated route shown on the evacuation plan. The room will reopen after the scheduled exercise. The archive report about an outbreak of violence belongs to the public affairs exhibition and is unrelated to today's drill. Visitor: Why was the session interrupted?
Noor: A drill was scheduled. I am sorry you missed the notice. The organiser is explaining the plan now.
Maya: Was the report about violence connected to it?
Noor: No. That was an archive document in the wrong folder. I have put it back.

readingBlocks.en: On the way out, Maya stopped at the evacuation plan on the corridor wall. The centre was preparing a supervised drill, and the organiser pointed to the designated route on the building's own plan. Participants would practise leaving together when asked to evacuate; the exercise was not an emergency. A visitor who had missed the explanation became angry about the temporary interruption. Noor tried to pacify him by listening to his concern and explaining when the room would reopen. She did not promise that his complaint would change the drill. On the reception desk lay an archive report about an outbreak of violence at an old public meeting. Maya asked why that report had been left beside the drill register. Noor moved it back into the exhibition folder. The report concerned a historical incident; it did not describe a present danger or the reason for today's drill.
readingBlocks.zh: 离开时，玛雅停在走廊墙上的撤离平面图前。中心正在准备由负责人组织的演练，组织者指出本楼平面图上的指定路线。参与者会练习接到要求后一起撤离；这是演练，并非紧急事件。一位没听到说明的访客因活动暂时中断而生气。努尔听他说明担忧，解释房间何时重新开放，试图安抚他，没有承诺投诉会改变演练。接待桌上放着一份历史报告，记述过去某次公众会议爆发的暴力。玛雅问它为何放在演练登记表旁。努尔把它放回展览文件夹。那份报告涉及历史事件，不说明眼前有危险，也不是今天演练的原因。

readingBlocks.en:
Scheduled drill
The organiser will explain the exercise and the designated route shown on the evacuation plan. The room will reopen after the scheduled exercise. The archive report about an outbreak of violence belongs to the public affairs exhibition and is unrelated to today's drill.
readingBlocks.zh:
预定演练
组织者会说明演练及撤离平面图上的指定路线。房间将在预定演练后重新开放。关于暴力爆发的历史报告属于公共事务展，与今天演练无关。

readingBlocks.en:
Visitor: Why was the session interrupted?
Noor: A drill was scheduled. I am sorry you missed the notice. The organiser is explaining the plan now.
Maya: Was the report about violence connected to it?
Noor: No. That was an archive document in the wrong folder. I have put it back.
readingBlocks.zh:
访客：为什么活动中断了？
努尔：安排了演练，很抱歉您没看到通知。组织者正在说明平面图。
玛雅：暴力事件报告与它有关吗？
努尔：没有，是一份放错文件夹的历史文献，我已经放回了。

glossary.note: 本例为人撤离的用法；evacuate people from a building 可表示疏散人员。
glossary.example: Participants would practise leaving when asked to evacuate.
glossary.exampleZh: 参与者会练习接到要求后撤离。

externalEvidence.definition: move out of an unsafe location into safety

glossary.note: 本场景是展示建筑路线的平面图；具体行动由该设施组织者说明。
glossary.example: Maya stopped at the evacuation plan on the corridor wall.
glossary.exampleZh: 玛雅停在走廊墙上的撤离平面图前。

glossary.note: an outbreak of violence；本条采用暴力爆发义，另有疾病暴发义。
glossary.example: The archive report described an outbreak of violence.
glossary.exampleZh: 历史报告记述一次暴力突然爆发。

externalEvidence.definition: a sudden violent spontaneous occurrence (usually of some undesirable condition)

glossary.note: 及物动词 pacify somebody；tried to 不保证已经成功。
glossary.example: Noor tried to pacify the visitor by listening to his concern.
glossary.exampleZh: 努尔听访客说明担忧，试图安抚他。

externalEvidence.definition: cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of

retrievalPrompts.function: The route drawn on the corridor wall
retrievalPrompts.cue: Describe the plan on the wall and the activity currently taking place.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 描述墙上的物件和正在进行的活动。
acceptableAnswers: The evacuation plan is on the corridor wall. Participants are practising how to evacuate in a supervised drill.

retrievalPrompts.function: The route drawn on the corridor wall
retrievalPrompts.cue: Correct the misunderstanding that the archive report describes a present incident.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 纠正把历史报告理解成眼前事件的误会。
acceptableAnswers: The report describes an outbreak of violence at an old meeting. It is unrelated to today's drill.

retrievalPrompts.function: The route drawn on the corridor wall
retrievalPrompts.cue: Describe the attempt to calm the visitor without assuming it succeeded.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 描述安抚访客的尝试，但不夸大效果。
acceptableAnswers: Noor tried to pacify the visitor by listening and explaining when the room would reopen.

transferPrompt.function: The route drawn on the corridor wall
transferPrompt.cue: A visitor is angry about a temporary gallery closure. Write one sentence about the receptionist's response.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 参观者因展馆暂时关闭而生气，写一句工作人员处理经过。
